lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: By mid-morning the heat had climbed into that dry weight that made thinking feel expensive. One of the donkeys started favoring its left hind leg just after they crossed a stretch of hardpan. BAH-lahg noticed first. He always did.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They stopped in the thin shade of a dead acacia that looked like it had argued with the wind for a century and finally lost. BAH-lahg crouched beside the animal, hands moving down the leg with the careful attention of someone who trusted what his fingers told him more than anything a person might say.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Strap's gone soft. Leather's cracking through.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek dropped his pack and knelt without being asked. He pulled the damaged strap free and turned it over. The leather had dried and split along the stress line where the buckle bit. Not finished yet, but another day of this heat and it would go completely.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He dug out a short length of braided cord and the small bronze awl he kept for quiet failures like this. The others watched while he worked. He scored the cracked section, cut away the worst of the dry edge, drove new holes, then rebound the strap in a tight overlapping pattern that would take the load better than the original leather ever had.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It wasn't pretty. It didn't need to be.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg rolled the repaired strap between his hands, pressing a thumb against every new stitch.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You always sew like you're angry.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looped the strap back through the buckle and cinched it tight around the pack frame. The leather creaked in protest but held.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: As if to object, the animal swung its head toward Zeek and gave a long, offended bray.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I think it agrees with BAH-lahg.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It always agrees with whoever isn't asking it to work.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg scratched the animal behind one ear.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You'd complain too if someone expected you to carry half a mountain through the desert.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: They're the easiest ones to verify.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For the first time since leaving the tomb, BAH-lahg laughed without forcing it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The sound caught all three of them by surprise.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It died almost as quickly as it had come.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek busied himself trimming one loose strand from the braided cord.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I'd forgotten what that sounded like.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The silence returned, but it no longer felt like something pressing on their shoulders. It settled beside them instead.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo picked up the strip of ruined leather and turned it over in her hands.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The crack ran almost perfectly through its center.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She rubbed her thumb along the brittle edge.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You know why leather fails here?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It was drying from the inside.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It fails long before it looks broken.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo slipped it into her pouch.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg tested the repair with two hard tugs and grunted.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo reached down, picked up the scrap of ruined leather Zeek had cut away, and slipped it into a pouch at her belt without comment. BAH-lahg noticed.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: What the hell do you want with that?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That was all she offered. She turned the scrap once between her fingers, then left it alone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They rested longer than the schedule allowed. The animals needed it more than anyone wanted to admit. Zeek sat with his back against the dead tree and took the journal out only long enough to confirm the last page hadn't changed. Three lines. No new ink. He closed it and, for the first time since the tomb, deliberately left it in the pack instead of keeping it against his ribs.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The decision felt small. It also felt like the first thing he had chosen rather than reacted to since the skeleton spoke his name.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg noticed him staring at nothing in particular.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Thinking about how much silver it takes to keep a mother in medicine and a crew in rope.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They moved on once the shadow of the acacia had shrunk to nothing useful. The repaired strap held. The donkeys settled into their usual sullen rhythm. The journal stayed in the pack, quiet for once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Late afternoon the wind shifted and brought the faintest smell of smoke and river mud. Uruk was still a day out, but the desert had started remembering there were cities in the world.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek flexed his left hand inside the linen. The mark was warm again. Not painful. Just present, like a second pulse that hadn't been invited.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not check the compass.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He already knew which way it pointed.
